output.brief:
The fall in incidents is not real. Analysts confirmed 37 incidents in September and 36 in October, in line with the roughly 38 a month before the migration. Brackwater's analyst jump host runs a script. About every five minutes it looks for confirmed incidents that are nearing the 4-hour containment deadline. It then moves each one to "Suspicious Activity–Monitoring", which the report doesn't count. This happened to 47 confirmed cases. None of the 47 has a recorded containment time, so they drop out of the containment and SLA figures. That is why Brackwater shows 100% containment and lower containment times. The platform connector did not write any categories, so this was not a software fault. Whether the script was deliberate is not yet established, but the pattern is consistent and automated. I'm confident about this. I did not establish whether the 28 retired detection rules are missing attacks.
Next steps:
- Do not cut the Halvard retainer.
- Do not pay the 60k bonus.
- Reinstate the 47 cases as incidents.
- Have your in-house team and Halvard check containment on each.
- Remove the integration role's category-edit rights.
- Ask Brackwater for a written explanation.
- Hold any service credit claim until containment is confirmed case by case.
- Review the dropped rules.
